notes: User references 2026-10-30: factory caption, writing on leg, curiosity close-up, poll card, offer collage. Angles nurse, Disney, plus-size. Dropped: invented-by-a-professional portrait (no real expert), 'sold out 3 times', 'ends tonight', 60%/57% off, free gift, 90-day guarantee, Buy now button, gross close-ups.

concepts.headline: WE SPENT 2 YEARS DESIGNING A SHOE FOR 12-HOUR SHIFTS.
concepts.angle: Factory proof: we spent 2 years designing a shoe for 12-hour shifts (no inventor/expert portrait, no sold-out claim)
concepts.based_on: User reference: 'This dentist invented a toothbrush... sold out 3 times' factory caption ad (expert and sold-out claims removed: not confirmed)
concepts.prompt: A real photo of a clean, bright shoe factory production line: long stainless-steel worktable with neat rows of finished shoes and black trays of soles stretching back, machines and fluorescent lights behind, softly blurred. In the foreground on the steel table, three single shoes from the product reference lined up diagonally: black-and-purple in front, then navy with bright blue accents, then red/burgundy, all sharp, exact, true proportions. Bottom: two stacked black caption boxes with white serif all-caps text, centered: "WE SPENT 2 YEARS DESIGNING" / "A SHOE FOR 12-HOUR SHIFTS." No person, no portrait. All text is large, bold and high contrast for readers aged 60+; nothing small or thin. Show all THREE shoes (black-and-purple, navy, red/burgundy). The ONLY text in the whole image is the two bottom caption boxes; the upper part of the photo has NO text at all. Never write anything about a dentist, a toothbrush, red light therapy or selling out.
concepts.revision: v2: v1 copied the reference's dentist/toothbrush headline and showed only 2 shoes

concepts.headline: I finished 3 12s without sore feet for the first time in years.
concepts.angle: Lo-fi handwriting on the leg after a run of shifts: first time in years without sore feet; 40% off today
concepts.based_on: User reference: 'I woke up without stiff joints...' written on the thigh + Emily RN winner testimonial ('up to 4 12s in a row')
concepts.prompt: A casual real smartphone photo from above: a woman's bare legs stretched out on a rumpled white bed in soft morning light, a coffee mug and a folded pair of navy scrubs on the nightstand. Handwritten in black marker on her upper thigh, in five short lines: "I finished 3 12s" / "without sore feet" / "for the first time" / "in years." then a short underline and "40% OFF TODAY" underlined. Next to her legs on the bed, a pair of the black-and-purple shoes from the product reference, sharp and correct. No other text. The ONLY words are the black marker handwriting on the thigh: no typed headline, no printed text anywhere.
concepts.revision: v2: v1 added a big typed headline duplicating the handwriting

concepts.headline: Most nurses don't know this trick for feet that swell by hour 10, but did you know…
concepts.angle: Curiosity caption: most nurses don't know this trick for feet that swell by hour 10 (stretch knit) with a sock-mark close-up
concepts.based_on: User reference: 'Most people don't know this trick keeps dust mites away... more' curiosity close-up (gross body close-up swapped for sock marks + shoe)
concepts.prompt: Top 30%: white background with a heavy black sans caption on three lines: "Most nurses don't know this trick" / "for feet that swell by hour 10," / "but did you know…" followed by grey text "more". Below, a real extreme close-up photo: a woman's ankle with deep red sock-elastic marks and slightly puffy skin, her fingers pressing on the sock line, and right next to her foot one navy shoe with bright blue accents from the product reference with a hand stretching its soft knit collar wide open to show the give, sharp and correct. Not gross, no wounds. All text is large, bold and high contrast for readers aged 60+; nothing small or thin.

concepts.headline: WHICH ONE MATTERS MOST ON A DISNEY DAY?
concepts.angle: Poll card: which feature matters most on a Disney park day
concepts.based_on: User reference: 'Which Biomax Pro upgrade matters most to you?' poll-card story ad
concepts.prompt: Background: a warm golden-hour real photo of a sunny theme-park street from a low angle, a woman about 60 in capri pants and the red/burgundy shoes from the product reference walking toward the camera (shoes sharp and correct), crowds and string lights softly blurred (no castles, no characters, no logos). Lower middle: a white rounded poll card with a black header strip and white all-caps text "WHICH ONE MATTERS MOST" / "ON A DISNEY DAY?", then four light-grey rounded option rows with dark text: "Cushion for 20,000 steps", "Room for feet that swell in the heat", "No laces to retie in line", "Slip-on for security checks". All text is large, bold and high contrast for readers aged 60+; nothing small or thin. The question appears ONLY once, inside the poll card's black header; the photo above the card has NO text.
concepts.revision: v2: v1 repeated the question as a big headline at the top

concepts.prompt: A warm, bright real kitchen photo: a smiling plus-size woman about 60 (clearly full-figured) sitting on a kitchen chair, leaning down to slip on one of the all-black shoes from the product reference (sharp, correct), the other shoe on the floor, morning sun, plants and a mug. Top center: a big heavy dark-brown two-line headline "Don't wait for" / "the heel pain.", then dark-brown bold text "Start supporting your feet now." Left: a red starburst with heavy white "40% OFF". Right: a round cream badge with a red ring and dark-red text "30-DAY MONEY-BACK GUARANTEE". Lower left: a cream ribbon label with dark-red all-caps "FREE SHIPPING". Lower right: a pair of the all-black shoes from the product reference standing on the counter, large and sharp. No buttons. All text is large, bold and high contrast for readers aged 60+; nothing small or thin.
